text:
mari: FYI, AcmeApp is seeing SSE chat streams that send an initial prefix then hang for ~5-20s before either resuming with the rest of the stream or the client reconnecting. Happening 1-2x/day for one customer. They captured a request_id: req_acme_0x9f23. Need reproducible curl + edge/app logs.
ben: can you paste the request_id + a minimal curl? which route/model?
ingrid: also include client UA and any proxy in front of the client. fast check: often buffering at proxy/nginx/fastly. HAR or ngrep would help.
mari: details below: request_id=req_acme_0x9f23, route=/v1/chat/stream, model=rwd-4o-std. Customer UA: "AcmeFrontend/2.1.0 (Electron)". They appear to go through Fastly (via headers). Minimal curl I gave them to try:
```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-4o-std","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream
```
ben: can you also paste the exact timestamp for the request? we need edge log correlation.
mari: timestamp they gave: 2026-03-10T09:18:42Z. App/server snippet around the req (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-10T09:18:42Z] INFO  handler.go:112 start request req_acme_0x9f23 route=/v1/chat/stream client=AcmeFrontend/2.1.0
[2026-03-10T09:18:42Z] DEBUG stream_writer.go:78 wrote prefix bytes=128 req=req_acme_0x9f23
[2026-03-10T09:18:54Z] WARN  stream_writer.go:122 write stalled duration=12s req=req_acme_0x9f23
[2026-03-10T09:19:00Z] INFO  stream_writer.go:145 wrote final bytes=640 req=req_acme_0x9f23
```
ingrid: that write-stalled line is useful. Can you get the Fastly/edge logs for that minute and a tcpdump from the worker if possible? also ask customer for a HAR from the client (chrome devtools).
seb: can ops pull edge logs for edge-7 around 09:18:40-09:19:05 for that req id? also kernel TCP stats would be useful (ESTABLISHED, retransmits).
deploy-bot: deploy notice: rwd-4o-std v12 rolled to prod-edge at 2026-03-10T09:20:00Z by @release-ci
ingrid: quick reproduction note — sometimes curl's internal buffering hides the prefix. try curl with --no-buffer and explicit Connection header. Example to try locally: 
```bash
curl -N --no-buffer -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Connection: keep-alive" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-4o-std","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"test streaming"}]}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream
```
mari: I ran that locally against a repro copy and saw: first chunk at 0.1s, then silence ~12s, then final chunk. ngrep snippet from the customer's run (times truncated):
```
09:18:42.120 GET /v1/chat/stream HTTP/1.1
09:18:42.254 SSE: data: {"delta":"Hello"}
09:18:54.260 (no packets)
09:19:00.512 SSE: data: {"delta":"...done"}
```
ben: OK collect everything into a tracepack: app logs, edge logs, tcpdump 30s centered on timestamp, HAR/ngrep, and the curl steps. @eng-infra can you generate a tracepack and drop a link?
mari: uploaded tracepack to internal S3: https://s3.redwood/tracepacks/1978887776-acme-sse-trace.tgz — contains edge.log, app.log (sanitized), tcpdump.pcap (30s), har.json, ngrep.txt. Credentials redacted in archive.
seb: I'll follow up with the customer to get their browser HAR and confirm if they have an intermediary (corporate proxy). assigning to @ingrid for initial analysis. :mag:
